newsitem.title: USA: Cross-border M & A set for record 1996 - study.
newsitem.headline: Cross-border M & A set for record 1996 - study.

text.p: Cross-border corporate transactions are set to break last year's record of $236.6 billion despite declining activity in some emerging markets, according to a study released Tuesday by KPMG Peat Marwick.

The robust activity of the year's first nine months are carrying over into the fourth quarter, most notably with the proposed more than $20 billion acquisition of MCI Communications Corp. by British Telecommunications Plc.
"Conditions for cross-border deals have never been better," said Steve Blum, a partner in the corporate finance section of KPMG.

In the first nine months of 1996, buyers spent $181.7 billion worldwide, compared with last year's $173.7 billion of cross-border acquisitions, joint ventures and minority investments, according to KPMG.
Despite the dollar increase, the number of transactions dropped 11 percent to 4,016, from 4,536 in the first three quarters of 1995.

KPMG said transactions targeting companies in China and India continued their sharp slowdowns, with 48 percent and 25 percent fewer such deals, respectively, compared with the first three quarters of 1995.
Meanwhile, the number of transactions into Latin America rose by 12 percent, with a 59 percent gain in deal value.
Russian firms were targeted 42 percent more often, but spending on those deals dropped by 83 percent as investors targeted smaller, more strategic transactions, Blum said.
The quarterly study of cross-border deals is based on announced transactions. Data for 1995 was adjusted for pricing changes, incompleted deals, and other factors.
